Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFIæ OF UNDERSEæTARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 08 May 2008 MAYOR FERNANDO Q. MIGUEL Koronadal City, South Cotabato Dear Mayor Miguel: This has reference to your earlier letter seeking our legal opinion on several queries pertaining to your enactment of that City's Annual Budget. the Sangguniang Panlungsod approved Per your letter, Appropriation Ordinance No. 12, Series of 2007 on 28 December 2007, CY 2008 Annual Budget. On 02 January 2008, the Sangguniang Panlungsod transmitted the same to your Office for your consideration. You approved said Ordinance but vetoed the item on Intelligence Services. Immediately thereafter, you transmitted said Appropriation Ordinance, together with the veto message, to the Sangguniang Panlungsod so that the latter may consider your veto message. Instead of overriding the vetoed item, the Sangguniang Panlungsod transmitted the Appropriation Ordinance, together with the veto message, to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for the latter's review. With such transmittal, you are of the view that the Sangguniang Panlungsod has already completed its legislative action in the adoption, passage and approval of the said Appropriation Ordinance and you can thus invoke Section 55 (b) of RA 7160, which provides that "the vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner herein provided; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriation ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed re-enacted". On 23 January 2008, you directed the City Budget Officer to release the full amount of five million pesos (Php 5,000,000.00) appropriation for Intelligence Services as this is the budget allocation for intelligence services in CY 2007 Annual Budget. Surprisingly, on 04 February 2008, the Sangguniang Panlungsod, with a vote of eight (8) members in favor and three (3) members against passed and approved SP Resolution No. 08, Series of 2008, entitled: "A Resolution Overriding the Item Veto of the City Mayor, Hon. Fernando Q. Miguel, on the Approved Appropriation for Intelligence Services Amounting to Seven Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 700,000.00) as embodied in the Annual Budget CY 2008 of the City of On 05 February 2008, the Sangguniang Panlungsod Koronadal". transmitted SP Resolution No. 08, Series of 2008, to your office for information. In view of the foregoing, you are now asking our legal opinion on the following queries, to wit:

-2- I) Are the procedures in the passage and approval of Appropriation Ordinance No. 12, series of 2007, including the item veto you made, consistent with existing laws? 2) Does the fact that the Sangguniang Panlungsod transmitted Appropriation Ordinance No. 12 to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan without making the necessary comments on the vetoed item mean that the said Ordinance has been approved in toto by the Sangguniang Panlungsod? Is Appropriation Ordinance No. 12, including the vetoed item for Intelligence Services, effective for all legal intents and purposes? Is it legal to invoke the re-enacted clause as prescribed in Section 55 (b) of RA 7160, thus, increasing the appropriations for intelligence services from Php 700,000 to Php 3) Are you entitled by law to cause the immediate release of the Intelligence Fund amounting to Php 5,000,000.00 pending review of the Appropriation Ordinance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan? 4) Was the passage by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of SP Resolution No. 08, Series of 2008 overriding the Item Veto on Intelligence Services proper and within the bounds of law, considering that said body has previously transmitted the Appropriation Ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review? Are the eight (8) votes mustered by the Sangguniang Panlungsod overriding the Item Veto of the Undersigned consistent with the 2/3 votes as what is prescribed in Section 55 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991?" Before dealing squarely with your queries, which we will answer jointly, we deem it proper to invite your attention to the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) applicable in the case at hand, to wit: -Section 319 "SECTION Legislative Authorization of the Budget.- On or before the end of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned shall enact, through an ordinance, the annual budget of the local government unit for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the local chief executive. -Section 54 ' 'SECTION 54. Approval of Ordinances.- (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal

-3- mayor, as the case may be. If the local chief executive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each and every page thereof; otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes. (b) The veto shall be communicated by the local chief executive concerned to the sanggunian within fifteen (15) days in the case of a province, and ten (IO) days in the case of a city or municipality; otherwise, the ordinance shall be deemed approved as if he had signed it. -Section 55 "Section 55. Veto Power of the Local Chief (a) The local chief executive may veto any Executive.- ordinance of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefor in writing. (b) The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall have the power to veto any particular item or items of an appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such a case, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner herein provided: otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted. (Emphasis Supplied) (c) The local chief executive may veto an ordinance or resolution only once. The sanggunian may override the veto of the local chief executive concerned by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all. its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned. -Section 320 The 320. Effectivity of Budgets.- ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing calendar year. xxx

The responsibility for the execution of the annual and supplemental budgets and the accountability therefor shall be vested primarily in the local chief executive concerned." -Section 56 "Section 56. Revi ew of Componen t City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang (a) Within three (3) days after approval, Panlalawigan . — the secretary to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (10) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlalawigan in making its decision. O If the sanggunian panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power , it shall conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod declare such ordinance or resolution in valid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panalalwigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Based on the foregoing, on or before the end of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned (the Sangguniang Panlungsod in your case) shall enact, through an ordinance, the annual budget of Koronadal City for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures you have submitted being the city mayor. The legislative instrument authorizing the budget is known as an Appropriation Ordinance. Said ordinance so enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod shall then be presented to you, as the city mayor, for your consideration. If you will approve the same, you shall affix your signature in each and every page thereof. Otherwise, you shall veto the entire appropriations

-5- ordinance or any item thereof and return it to the Sangguniang Panlungsod with your message citing your objections. Veto is defined as the refusal of assent by the executive officer whose assent is necessary to perfect a law which has been passed by the legislative body and the message which is usually sent to such body by the executive, stating such refusal and the reasons therefore (Black's Law Dictionary, 5thed., 1983). As a general rule, the veto by the local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall be on the entire ordinance. The reason being that all provisions of an ordinance (other than an appropriation ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program) relate to one subject matter and therefore correlated. If any of the provisions is stricken out, the substantive aspect of the ordinance shall be greatly affected. An exception however is found under Section 55(b) of the Local Government Code where the local chief executive is authorized to make an item veto on appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program. The reason being that one item in an appropriations ordinance, among others, is different from the other items therein so that if any of those is vetoed, the substantive aspect of the appropriation ordinance is not affected. In such item veto, it must be stressed that only the vetoed item/s (in your case, those pertaining to Intelligence Services) shall not be given force and effect. Those item/s, which are not vetoed or objected to (items which you approved), shall not be affected and thus enforceable. It must be stressed further that the item veto by the local chief executive should be spelled out in writing (which you actually did vis-å-vis the Sangguniang Panlungsod) so that the sanggunian concerned may properly consider it and decides to override it or not. The aforesaid overriding power is accorded to the sanggunian as part of the checks and balances between the legislative and executive branches of the government (the city government in your case) and, at the same time, as a remedy of the sanggunian to give effect to those item/s previously vetoed by the local chief executive. The manner in which the sanggunian may exercise its overriding power is laid down under the aforequoted Section 55 0 which provides that if the sanggunian shall override the veto of the local chief executive, the same may be done by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned. Once overridden by the Sanggunian, the vetoed ordinance •or any item thereof shall no longer be presented to the local chief executive for approval as it already becomes deemed approved by operation of law, even without the approval of the latter. On the other hand, if the sanggunian fails to override the veto, the item/s in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, (the item on Intelligence Services in your case) shall be deemed reenacted. We are of the view that such failure to override the veto might come in two (2) ways, namely, (a) as a result of the sanggunian's failure to muster the vote of two-thirds (2/3) of all its members, and (2) if the sanggunian deems it proper not to exercise at all its

-6- overriding power and thus waived to exercise the same by simple inaction. When the Sangguniang Panlungsod received the Appropriation Ordinance together with your veto message setting forth the reasons for your item veto on Intelligence Services, they should have overridden your item veto by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without your approval pursuant to Section 550 of the Code. What they did however was that they transmitted the Appropriation Ordinance, together with your veto message, to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review. In this regard, we concur with your view that the act of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, that of transmitting the Appropriation Ordinance, together with your veto message to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review when they should have instead exercised their veto power, signifies that the Sangguniang Panlungsod has already completed their adoption, passage and approval of the said Appropriation Ordinance. Otherwise stated, such act of transmitting the Appropriation Ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan means that so far as their level is concerned, the Sangguniang Panlungsod has already completed the budget authorization phase in the local government budget process. The budget authorization phase starts from the time the local chief executive submits the budget to the sanggunian for legislative deliberation and ends with the corresponding enactment of the appropriations ordinance (DBM Updated Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units, p. 60). The submission of the Appropriation Ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the reviewing body, commences the budget review phase (Ibid., p. 70). Also, their transmittal of the Appropriation Ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan means that the Sangguniang Panlungsod deemed not to exercise at all its overriding power and thus waived the exercise of the same. The Sangguniang Panlungsod's failure to exercise its overriding power vis-ä-vis your item veto has the effect of reenacting the item on Intelligence Services in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year. May we respectfully stress that pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, approved items as well as those reenacted in the Appropriation Ordinance can be validly enforced so that funds corresponding thereto can already be disbursed because effectivity is determined not upon review thereof but rather in accordance with Section 320 of the Code which as mandated therein, is effective at the beginning of the ensuing year. Thus, if the appropriations for Intelligence Services in the previous year amounted to five million pesos (Php 5,000,000.00) and the vetoed appropriation for the ensuing year amounts to only seven hundred thousand (Php700,OOO.OO), pursuant to our discussion above, the former appropriation shall be enforced it being the consequence of the reenactment of the item in the previous budget under Section 55 (b). Let it be noted that notwithstanding the waiver of its overriding power, the Sangguniang Panlungsod surprisingly still passed and approved SP Resolution No. 08, Series of 2008, entitled: "A Resolution Overriding the Item Veto of the City Mayor, Hon. Fernando Q. Miguel, on the Approved Appropriation for Intelligence Services Amounting to Seven Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 700,000.00) as embodied in the Annual Budget CY 2008 of the City of Koronadal". Such passage and approval is legally

infirmed as the Sangguniang Panlungsod, as discussed above, has already waived the exercise of its overriding power. Be that as it may, since the subject Resolution has already been passed in accordance with the procedural requirements set by the Local Government Code, it thus enjoys the presumption of validity, which means that your item veto on Intelligence Services is considered to have been validly overridden by the Sangguniang Panlungsod. Thus, the appropriations for Intelligence Services for the ensuing year amounting to only seven hundred thousand (Php700,OOO.OO) shall be enforced. Finally, if you are nonetheless determined to question the substantive validity of the subject Resolution using as grounds our discussion above, you may file an action for Declaratory Relief in accordance with Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. Please be informed that this Department is bereft of any authority to declare invalid any measure passed by local sanggunians. Only courts can make such declaration. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADER Undersecreta LegaU09:17 cc: Director Buagas B.
